free_agency: Free Agency Review Home   >   2026 Ultimate Draft Kit   >  UDK – Free Agency Review Fantasy implications for the biggest offseason moves QB RB WR TE Free Agents re-signed Daniel Jones Re-signed | 29 Years Old IND | 2 years, $88 million Danny Dimes went to Indy last year to challenge Anthony Richardson for the starting gig, and not only did he win that job in camp, he had his team headed towards a top seed in the AFC until...Week 14. Unfortunately, the Colts' season went south real quick after Jones tore his Achilles. When he was the starter in Weeks 1-13, the Colts were 8-4, and Jones was the QB7 in fantasy. Talk about a late-round value, especially in SuperFlex leagues! Entering 2026, Jones is back in Indy after the Colts used the transition tag on him then re-signed him to a new two-year deal worth up to $100 million. For fantasy, with much of his value tied to his ability to contribute with his legs, it remains to be seen if 2026 will be as successful for Jones given his Achilles injury. The front office and coaching staff is essentially betting their jobs and Jones returning to form. We'll see! signed Malik Willis Signed | 27 Years Old MIA | 3 years, $67.5 million Willis' time in Tennessee was pretty forgettable to say the least. The team took him in the third round back in 2022 and moved on after just three starts in two years. However, he landed in Green Bay as Jordan Love's backup and now has a chance to revitalize his career as a starter after getting some great coaching from Matt LaFleur. We've seen other young QBs (Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, Daniel Jones, for example) take similar paths: Dumped by their original organization, sit and learn for a couple of years as a backup, and then get a second chance at a starting gig elsewhere. Could Willis be next? He lands in Miami with new head coach Jeff Hafley, who comes over from the Packers, so this signing makes a lot of sense. For fantasy, the Dolphins project to be among the worst teams in the league, but we know what works at the QB position for the game we play - elite rushing upside, and Willis certainly has the wheels to put up fantasy friendly numbers on the ground. signed Kyler Murray Signed | 29 Years Old MIN | 1 year, $1.3 million The Kyler Murray era in Arizona is officially coming to a close with the Cardinals set to move on. Still just 28 years old, Kyler will look to get his career back on track in Minnesota, perhaps following the path of guys like Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold. This move makes all the sense in the world for Kevin O'Connell's team. They're short on cash this year in terms of cap space, and with Arizona picking up the vast majority of is salary this year, they were able to sign him for the vet minimum. Expect the team to frame this as a QB competition throughout the summer, but if you watched JJ "Nine" McCarthy play NFL football in 2025, you likely know where this is headed in terms of the Week 1 starter. signed Tua Tagovailoa Signed | 28 Years Old ATL | 1 year The Dolphins and Mike McDaniel had some nice seasons there in Miami, but they couldn't get over the hump, and as a result, the franchise is undergoing a facelift this offseason with a brand new GM and head coach. The previous regime gave Tua a four-year, $212 million deal a couple of years back, and now the Tua era is officially over as the team is designating him as a post-June 1 cut. It's going to hurt, but Miami is going the Russell Wilson route and eating a ton of dead money as they look to rest the franchise. In fact, they're eating an NFL record $99M in dead money over the next two seasons. Looking for some insurance for Michael Penix coming off a torn ACL, the Falcons signed another lefty to a cheap one-year deal with the Dolphins paying the vast majority of his salary. signed Kirk Cousins Signed | 38 Years Old LV | 1 year, $11.3 million Kirko Chainz' agent is the GOAT. This man just keeps getting fully guaranteed deals and cashing those checks. He's made over $320 million in his career...sheesh! Good for you, Kirk. The Raiders signed Cousins to what is essentially a one-year deal worth about $20 million given that the Falcons are picking up some of the salary for 2026. He'll mentor Fernando Mendoza and potentially even start for part of the season while the Raiders groom there eventual franchise QB. For fantasy, Cousins is obviously not the prolific passer he used to be, but hopefully he can keep the offense on track to ensure Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty deliver for our fantasy rosters. re-signed Aaron Rodgers Re-signed | 42 Years Old PIT | 1 year, up to $25 million Rodgers spent the majority of last offseason pondering his NFL future before landing in Pittsburgh on a one-year deal with Mike Tomlin. In classic Steelers fashion, Rodgers did enough to help them stay competitive and make the playoffs, but they ultimately fell short in the Wild Card Round. At this point in his career, the vet isn't really on the radar for fantasy outside of 2QB formats. Now 42 years old, Rodgers and the Steelers seemed like a one-year fling, but they hired his old coach, Mike McCarthy, to replace Tomlin, so they'll reunite one last time while Pittsburgh. We're not expecting Rodgers to suddenly turn back the clock and support multiple high-end fantasy options, but he's certainly a better option than guys like Drew Allar or Will Howard. re-signed Marcus Mariota Re-signed | 32 Years Old WAS | 1 year, $7 million The former Oregon Duck has spent the last two seasons in Washington as Jayden Daniels' backup, and when Daniels has missed time because of injury, Mariota has filled in admirably. Washington re-signed him to a one-year deal in free agency to keep some continuity in the QB room. For fantasy, we've seen him continue to post usable numbers when he's been under center, thanks mainly to his ability to run. In seven full stars last year with the Commanders, Mariota averaged 17.2 fantasy points per game, giving him life as a streamer if and when his number gets called. Russell Wilson Unsigned | 37 Years Old Russ was named the starter in New York coming out of camp, but we all knew it was a matter of when, not if, Jaxson Dart would take over. The most cringe QB in the league only lasted three games before the rook got his shot and ran away with the job. This is probably where the road ends for Mr. Unliiiiimited. He says he believes he can still be a starter in the league, but after bouncing around from Denver to Pittsburgh to New York the last three years, it sure feels like the NFL says otherwise. Free Agents re-signed Breece Hall Re-Signed | 25 Years Old NYJ | 3 years, $45.8 million It feels like Breece has already lived nine lives in the NFL (playing for the Jets will do that), but he's still not even 25 years old. One of the most productive and efficient backs over the last three seasons, the Jets rewarded Breece with a brand new three-year deal worth just over $15 million per year. Some dynasty managers out there may have been hoping for Breece to finally be unleashed on a new team and hopefully better offense, but this contract says he'll get plenty of volume in New York. We're not all that optimistic about the team in 2026, but if they can land a stud QB in next year's draft, perhaps New York can finally get it going and unlock Breece's full potential. signed Kenneth Walker Signed | 25 Years Old KC | 3 years, up to $45 million Ken Bone! Walker was a key piece of the Seattle offense on their Super Bowl run, and now that Zach Charbonnet is coming off a January ACL injury, the Seahawks have a major need at RB with Walker hitting free agency. Usually, in situations like this, where the team has so much success, they look to bring back key contributors, but Walker hit the open market and got a big old bag of money from the Chiefs, signing a 3-year deal worth just over $14M per year. He's still only 25 years old and remains one of the best home run hitters in the game, something that was severely lacking in KC's run game over the last two years. For context, over the last two years Chiefs RBs have run for 10+ yards less than 9% of the time, 31st amongst 32 teams. Enter Walker, who was third in the league last season in rate of 10+ yard runs. He'll bring stability to the backfield and should be heavily featured, especially with Mahomes coming off the ACL. signed Travis Etienne Jr. Signed | 27 Years Old NO | 4 yrs, up to $52 million Etienne bounced back from a disappointing 2024 season and was one of the biggest values in 2025 drafts, given the uncertainty around his role and standing on the depth chart with the new staff under Liam Cohen. Despite being drafted outside of the top-24 RBs, Etienne finished as the RB10 thanks to his workhorse volume. He was one of just 13 backs a year ago with 300+ total opportunities, and after that bounce-back season, he was rewarded in free agency with a multi-year deal with the Saints. re-signed Javonte Williams Re-Signed | 26 Years Old DAL | 3 years, $24 million One of the best fantasy stories in 2025 has to be the resurgence of Javonte Williams as Dallas' RB1. His career got derailed by that complex ACL injury in his second season as a Bronco, but the talent was never the question. Now healthy, we saw what made Javonte such an exciting prospect coming out of UNC. Among qualified RBs, Javonte was fourth in yards after contact per attempt, and he was one of just 10 NFL backs with double-digit rushing scores. After a bounce-back season, Dallas rewarded him with a 3-year extension that includes $16 million in guaranteed money. He'll be the Cowboys' bell cow for the next couple of seasons after averaging almost 19 total opportunities per game last year. re-signed J.K. Dobbins Re-signed | 27 Years Old DEN | 2 years, up to $20 million What a fun story Dobbins was in 2024 and then again in 2025. After tearing his Achilles in Week 1 of 2023, he signed a league minimum deal with the Chargers that included just $50K in guarantees, yet played a 63% of the snaps in 2024. The long-term durability is still a big concern, especially considering he missed four weeks with a sprained MCL in his surgically reconstructed knee in 2024 then spent the final two months on IR with a season-ending foot injury in 2025. Dobbins proved these last two years that he can at function in a timeshare. He's back with Sean Payton and Denver on a two-year deal, forming a committee with last year's second-rounder RJ Harvey. While we still expect Harvey to see high-value looks in the pass game, Dobbins should have FLEX-worthy weeks in the right matchup while running behind one of, if not the, best offensive lines in football. signed Rico Dowdle Signed | 28 Years Old PIT | 2 yrs, up to $12 million After Chuba got hurt last year, Rico essentially stole the RB1 role in Carolina, and he was productive with his opportunities. Mr. "Two Pumps" Dowdle rushed for 1,076 yards this past season and ran for a career high six TDs as the leader of the committee in Carolina. Dowdle has been the lead guy for two different teams now, and while he may not be an elite talent, the guy just gets the job done. During the last two years in Dallas and Carolina, he's shown he can be reliable with 200+ touches in a season. He lands in Pittsburgh reunited with Mike McCarthy teamming up with Jaylen Warren. signed Kenny Gainwell Signed | 27 Years Old TB | 2 years, up to $14 million It pays to be in Aaron Rodgers' inner circle, just ask Kenny G! He signed a one-year deal worth just under $2M last offseason after spending the first part of his career in Philly as a third-down back and kick returner. Of course, most of us weren't expecting much from Gainwell given his track record and the minimal investment, but goodness gracious, he was a force in PPR formats thanks to his team-leading 73 receptions. The only backs with more catches? CMC, Bijan, and Jahmyr Gibbs. The Buccaneers signed Gainwell to a 2-year deal to mix in with Bucky Irving. He will never be a workhorse in the league, but he offers an NFL franchise a valuable skill set as a pass catcher out of the backfield. signed Tyler Allgeier Signed | 26 Years Old ARI | 2 yrs, $12 million Allgeier has spent the last couple of seasons as the 'thunder' to Bijan Robinson's 'lightning' in Atlanta. A dependable early-down runner who's been productive at the goal line, Allgeier was going to mix in a Arizona backfield alongside Trey Benson and James Conner. However, the Cardinals threw a curve ball and drafted Jeremiyah Love 3rd overall. Sorry Tyler! For fantasy, he probably remains a rosterable FLEX with benefits, similar to what we saw over the last couple of years with the Falcons. signed Chris Rodriguez Jr. Signed | 25 Years Old JAX | 2 years, $10 million CROD! Rodriguez landed a nice two-year deal with the Jaguars in free agency, signing for $6.2M guaranteed. It may not seem like a ton, but considering he got more guaranteed money than Rico Dowdle, the money says he could have a role in Liam Coen's offense. He played his college ball at Kentucky when Liam Coen was on the staff, and in that season, he logged 238 touches. He hasn't really done much in the NFL thus far, but the familiarity in Coen's system and guaranteed money at least adds some threat to Bhayshul Tuten's early-down role in 2026. signed Emanuel Wilson Signed | 27 Years Old SEA | 1 year, $2.1 million After losing Ken Walker in free agency and Zach Charbonnet to a torn ACL in mid January during their Super Bowl run, there's a massive opportunity up for grabs in this Seahawks backfield. The team spent a late 1st on Jadarian Price who should eventually be the lead back. Wilson, who's 26 years old, is coming off a career high 142 total opportunities as Josh Jacobs' backup last season in Green Bay and flashed in a major way with his lone start in Week 12 with Jacobs sidelined. signed Keaton Mitchell Signed | 24 Years Old LAC | 2 years, $9.25 million After flashing off and on over the last couple of years in Baltimore behind Derrick Henry, Keaton Mitchell lands in LA on a two-year deal with $5M guaranteed. He brings a speed element to Mike McDaniel's scheme and is a great fit in the offense given his burst and big play ability on the edge. He's likely to slide in as the RB2 behind Omarion Hampton and could be one of fantasy's top insurance backs for an offense that should win plenty of games. signed Rachaad White Signed | 27 Years Old WAS | 1 year, $2 million 'Dick White,' as he's known around TFFB HQ, is going to be donning new colors in 2026 after spending the first four years of his career in Tampa. White was the guy a couple of seasons ago, but he was relegated to a change-of-pace option with the emergence of the more efficient Bucky Irving and Sean Tucker over the last two years. For context, his opportunities per game have declined from 20.1 to 12.6 to 10.4 over the last three seasons. Already 27 years old, White gets a short-term deal to join a committee in Washington where he can specialize as a pass catcher and in pass protection while playing with his former college QB in Jayden Daniels. signed Isiah Pacheco Signed | 27 Years Old DET | 1 year He burned too bright! Pacheco is the perfect example of what can happen to a Day 3 back in the NFL. Despite being the workhorse for Andy Reid during the back half of his rookie year and during his second season, Pacheco was never the same after he fractured his fibula in 2024, and ultimately, he ended up in a time share with Kareem Hunt. Given that the former seventh-rounder is coming off yet another injury-plagued and inefficient season, his future for fantasy is murky at best. He lands in Detroit on a one-year deal to backup Jahmyr Gibbs. signed Brian Robinson Signed | 27 Years Old ATL | 1 year, $2.5 million B Rob was the early down back in Washington in 2023 and 2024, but the team moved off him in favor of BILL CROSKEY, sending him to San Francisco via trade just before the start of the season. With CMC seeing a million opportunities and staying healthy all year (#Blessed), Robinson was nothing more than a backup in 2025 as he appeared on just 17% of the offensive snaps. He was an older prospect coming out of Bama, so he's already entering his age-27 season. The market wasn't hot and heavy for Robinson, so he landed in Atlanta on a cheap one-year deal. Obviously, this is the Bijan show (don't click the wrong B Rob in your draft!), but with Tyler Allgeier vacating almost 160 opportunities, Brian could have a role behind Bijan. We don't anticipate much consistent production as long as Bijan is healthy, but Brian becomes of the few high priority backups late in drafts. Joe Mixon Unsigned | 30 Years Old Congratulate yourself for scoring as many fantasy points as Joe Mixon in 2025. The Texans cut the veteran for only $2 million and save themselves a solid $8 million against the cap. He will be entering his ninth year in the league at age 30 and coming off a mysterious foot injury, which is not ideal for a free agent RB. After the team traded for David Montgomery, Mixon's NFL future hangs in the balance. Kareem Hunt Unsigned | 31 Years Old Kareem Hunt is like those three-day-old leftovers in the back of your fridge. Will it get the job done for dinner if you are hungry? Sure. Are you going to impress your guests after popping that Tupperware in the microwave? Of course not. If your NFL team needs a 30-year-old back who can pile up touches en route to 3.5 yards per carry and a cloud of dust, Hunt is your guy. Nick Chubb Unsigned | 30 Years Old What's the saying? "Don't cry because it's over, smile because it happened." Let's remember the good times for Mr. Chubb. One of the most dominant runners in the league over the last decade, the wily old veteran is now entering the final stage of his NFL career. After Joe Mixon's mysterious foot injury caused him to miss the entire season, Houston signed him to a one-year deal last year, and ultimately, he was phased out as the year went on. If you're a fan of Nick Chubb, it was at least awesome to see him play a full season one more time after he suffered that nasty second knee injury in 2023, then broke his foot in 2024. Perhaps he lands a one-year deal for an NFL team shopping on the value menu, but it wouldn't be surprising for him to be a guy who signs late in the process as he weighs his NFL future. Free Agents franchise George Pickens Franchise Tag | 25 Years Old DAL | 1 year, $27.3 million Back up the Brinks truck. George made himself a pile of cash this year, showcasing the type of weekly boom potential and alpha status teams dream of at the WR position. Pickens had five weeks inside the top 10 and led the league in receiving yards off slant routes. He is a game breaker, and we expect Jerry Jones to work out a long-term deal. They used the franchise tag on George as a place holder, but expect something in the neighborhood of $30+ million if he strikes a multi-year contract. signed Mike Evans Signed | 33 Years Old SF | 3 years, up to $60.4 million As they, "All good things must come to an end." It's going to be really weird seeing the future Hall-of-Famer where a different jersey in 2026, but Mike Evans is officially headed for San Francisco. The 32-year-old vet only played in eight games last year due to multiple injuries (hamstring, broken collarbone, and concussion), so this signing does come with some risk, but he's still one of the top X receivers in the game. Ever since the Brandon Aiyuk fiasco and Ricky Pearsall health issues, this offense has been searching for that missing component on the outside, so perhaps Evans can fill that void and help take this team over the top. signed Alec Pierce Signed | 26 Years Old IND | 4 years, $116 million Of all the WR free agents in this year's class, Alec Pierce might have made himself the most amount of money showing out in 2025. Forever known as a "Cardio King" running deep routes, he seemed like the go-to WR for Daniel Jones for mos
coaching: Offseason Coaching Changes Home   >   2026 Ultimate Draft Kit   >  UDK – Coaching Changes Loading... Fantasy Implications for Coaching Moves This Offseason Head Coach Mike LaFleur, ARI The younger LaFleur brother comes to the desert after years soaking up knowledge in the McVay and Shanahan coaching systems. The Cardinals averaged 40 pass attempts per game in Jacoby Brissett starts last year and project to be among the worst teams in the NFL, currently sitting at 4.5 for their win total. We expect that passing volume to slightly come down as he integrates third overall pick Jeremiyah Love into the offense. Head Coach Kevin Stefanski, ATL The former two-time NFL Coach of the Year was let go in Cleveland and now finds a home in Atlanta. Good luck, Kevin! The Falcons have not had a winning season since 2017, the second-longest streak in the NFL. His offenses consistently were among the best at running the football, ranking top 10 in rush attempts every year from 2019 to 2023. All-Pro RB Bijan Robinson is the centerpiece, but the question remains if you have two QBs (Tua & Penix), do you truly have none? Head Coach Jesse Minter, BAL The former Chargers defensive coordinator takes over for long-time legend John Harbaugh. He looks to bring the same intensity on the defensive side of the ball; hopefully, with a full season from QB Lamar Jackson and one last run from fantasy legend Derrick Henry. The Ravens are the favorites in a tough AFC North projected for 10.5 wins. Head Coach Joe Brady, BUF Apparently, sporting a 12-5 record was not good enough for Bills ownership, as long-time HC Sean McDermott was axed and Brady was promoted from offensive coordinator. The Bills led the NFL in rush attempts inside the red zone as Josh Allen and James Cook formed an incredible duo. The question will be if the acquisition of DJ Moore helps the WR room progress forward, and the Bills finally break through in the AFC playoffs. Head Coach Todd Monken, CLE At 60 years old, this is Monken’s first head-coaching gig in the NFL after being an offensive coordinator for Baltimore the last two years and numerous other stops. The data is not kind to old head coaches: among eight first-time head coaches over the last 25 years that were 55+ years old, they averaged 6.4 wins in Year 1, and only two of those coaches lasted more than three years. Monken is inheriting a team of brown-stained pants that punted the ball (93 times) more than any other team in the NFL and averaged just 5.0 yards per attempt. Woof. The QB play is a massive question mark moving forward. Head Coach Klint Kubiak, LV Kubes! After leading the Seahawks offense to a Super Bowl title, Kubiak was the prized coaching hire of the off-season. He will need to fix a Raiders offense that was dead last in points and yards per game last season. In fact, the team had five total rushing TDs on the season! Expect No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza to slowly be integrated as he holds the clipboard behind Kirk Cousins. Oh, and expect Brock Bowers to see 10+ targets a game. Head Coach Jeff Hafley, MIA After two seasons as the Green Bay defensive coordinator, Hafley takes over in Miami for a team that clearly is rebuilding. The Dolphins' defense is a project after allowing the third-highest completion percentage (72%) in NFL history last year. After drafting offensive line and defensive pieces early in the draft, fantasy managers will need to have patience as everyone but De’Von Achane is a mystery to us. Head Coach John Harbaugh, NYG Depending on who you talk to, Harbaugh is either a living legend (most road playoff wins in NFL history) or someone who fell short of expectations (just one Super Bowl). Regardless, he represents a major culture change in New York for a team with an exciting core of offensive players (Dart-Skattebo-Nabers) and a nasty pass rush on defense. Depending on the recovery timeline for their offensive stars, the Giants are on our short list of teams that could surprise in 2026. Head Coach Mike McCarthy, PIT Haven’t we seen this movie before? Mike McCarthy, former Green Bay and Dallas head coach, ventures to another storied NFL franchise, potentially reuniting with his buddy Aaron Rodgers. It will be strange to see a non-Mike Tomlin coach on the sidelines as the Steelers routinely outperformed expectations. For 2026, keep in mind Pittsburgh has a “first-place schedule” adding games against Denver and road games in New England and Philadelphia. Woof. Head Coach Robert Saleh, TEN After piecing together a broken 49ers defense last year, Saleh was hired in Tennessee to right the ship for an organization desperate to regain their edge. The Titans' offense was tied or trailing on 84% of their offensive snaps in a mostly abysmal season for No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward. The Titans find themselves in a highly competitive AFC South, albeit with the arrow pointing up on their potential. Offensive Coordinator Nathaniel Hackett, ARI Do not ask us how this man continues to be employed in the NFL. The former OC and one-year failed head coach experiment in Denver was a “defensive analyst” last year in Green Bay. This is LaFleur’s ship, and Hackett is aboard simply to provide his offensive “expertise”, whatever that means. Offensive Coordinator Tommy Rees, ATL The former Notre Dame QB follows Kevin Stefanski from Cleveland and will be calling plays for the Falcons. The offensive play-makers between Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts are certainly top-tier, but the Falcons’ success will ultimately come down to the QB play. Both Stefanski and Rees have mentioned establishing a “wide zone” run scheme throughout their press conferences. Offensive Coordinator Declan Doyle, BAL After a year as Ben Johnson’s offensive coordinator in Chicago, the 30-year-old Doyle will be calling plays in Baltimore. The Ravens ran the ball on 55% of their “early downs” (the highest rate in the NFL) as the Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry combo remains the heartbeat of the offense. Baltimore does have to replace a number of key pieces on the offensive line, fullback Patrick Ricard, and two TEs, so perhaps we see some innovation in 3-wide sets for 2026. Offensive Coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr., BUF The former long-time Saints offensive coordinator latches on to Buffalo serving under Joe Brady, someone who was Carmichael’s offensive assistant back in New Orleans. This is Brady’s offense so Pete is OC in title only. Offensive Coordinator Press Taylor, CHI Zac Taylor’s younger brother will have the esteemed privilege of being Ben Johnson’s “yes man” in Chicago. He is being promoted from passing game coordinator to OC but play-calling duties remain with Johnson. The Bears jumped from 28th in points per game (18.2) to 9th (25.9) in 2025; that is the 6th largest year-to-year jump (7.7 ppg) over the last decade. Offensive Coordinator Travis Switzer, CLE The former Baltimore run-game coordinator follows Todd Monken to Cleveland in hopes of fixing an offense that completed just 57.9% of their passes last year. That putrid passing mark ranks 305th out of 320 NFL teams over the last decade. The Browns did add several high-end WRs in the draft, hoping to give the team more pass-catching threats than just TE Harold Fannin Jr. and the WR formerly known as Jerry Jeudy. Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb, DEN The 31-year-old Webb was a hot commodity this offseason, interviewing with multiple teams for the head coaching positions. Instead, he remains in Denver and gets elevated to OC. Sean Payton declared that Webb will be taking over play-calling duties, trying to restore some of the passing efficiency numbers for Bo Nix. Offensive Coordinator Drew Petzing, DET Affectionately known as the “Blob Fish” on our podcast, Petzing parlayed a couple of years in the Arizona desert to another OC job alongside Dan Campbell. The Lions had a massive drop in rushing efficiency last year after Ben Johnson left town. Petzing’s goal will be to “restore the roar” of a top-5 scoring offense and take advantage of their “fourth place schedule”. Trey McBride came out after the hire and said Petzing’s scheme could mean great things for Sam LaPorta in Detroit. Offensive Coordinator Eric Bieniemy, KC The longtime KC offensive coordinator in the early Patrick Mahomes era (2018-2022) returns after three different jobs in three years. This offense needs a facelift after Kansas City had four total offensive plays of 20+ yards that resulted in a TD last year, tied for the fewest in the NFL. The running game was also pitiful, producing just one total 20+ yard run on the season. The arrival of Kenneth Walker III should help, but the Chiefs' overall offensive ceiling depends on Mahomes’ return from a major injury. Offensive Coordinator Mike McDaniel, LAC Love him or hate him, McDaniel is a lightning rod for fantasy production. The former Dolphins head coach will have tons of weapons at his disposal and hopefully a full, healthy offensive line. The Chargers will not want Justin Herbert to repeat last year when he led all QBs in rushing yards via scrambles, and led the league in % of pressured dropbacks (43%). Expect even ancillary speed threats like Keaton Mitchell and rookie Brenen Thompson to be worked in alongside main fantasy options of Omarion Hampton and Ladd McConkey. This offense is going to be one of our favorites to keep an eye on in training camp and pre-season. Offensive Coordinator Nate Scheelhaase, LAR The Rams' offensive coordinator position is an honorary title, as Sean McVay is the one who rules the roost. However, keep in mind the running list of current head coaches in the league who have recently held this position: Mike LaFleur, Liam Coen, Kevin O’Connell, Matt LaFleur… Scheelhaase has rave reviews from many throughout the league, so do not be surprised if he is on the short list of potential head coaches in 2027. Offensive Coordinator Andrew Janocko, LV Janocko (pronounced juh-NO-co) is a Klint Kubiak buddy who was with him in their last couple of stops in Seattle, New Orleans, and Minnesota. He follows him to Las Vegas to try to fix an offense that averaged just 11.5 points per game on the road last year, by far the worst in the NFL. Janocko’s reputation as QB whisperer will come in handy in developing No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza and keeping Kirk Cousins flush with Kohl’s Cash. Offensive Coordinator Bobby Slowik, MIA Slowik was a hot commodity in coaching circles after guiding C.J. Stroud to a breakout rookie season in 2023. However, things headed south the following year, and he was let go. After spending a year as Miami’s senior passing game coordinator, he was promoted to offensive coordinator and play-caller under this new Dolphins regime. Bobby will have his work cut out for him connecting new QB Malik Willis with a group of barf-worthy pass-catching options. Seriously, stop what you are doing right now and go look at the Dolphins' WR depth chart. Apologies for what you are about to see. Offensive Coordinator Matt Nagy, NYG He’s back! The man known as the “Budget Magician” on our podcast moves from offensive coordinator in Kansas City to play-caller in New York. The Giants have some exciting young pieces, as the offense was competitive in almost every Jaxson Dart start last year. The team quietly ranked top half in points per game and yards per game, and with a bit of injury luck, you can see a path forward for this team being in the mix in the NFC East. Offensive Coordinator Frank Reich, NYJ Reich wins the title of oldest offensive coordinator (64 years young) in the league, which is wild considering the average age of the other 31 OCs is 41 years. We are not quite sure if Aaron Glenn and the Jets front office had an updated resume for Reich, as he was out of the NFL for the last two years. We would put the odds quite low that he remains in this position for 2027. Offensive Coordinator Sean Mannion, PHI The Eagles are a funny bunch as they have ping-ponged from Super Bowl years (2022 & 2024) to playoff disappointments (2023 & 2025) recently. Part of the equation was the offensive coordinator position changing every single year. Mannion is an up-and-coming name from the Packers coaching tree. He will be bent on restoring Saquon Barkley and the Eagles' big-play rushing offense, alongside a bevy of new pass-catchers in the mix. He will be taking over play-calling duties as Nick Sirianni remains in his “CEO-coaching” style. Offensive Coordinator Brian Angelichio, PIT The former Vikings passing game coordinator joins Mike McCarthy in Pittsburgh. One quote from a front office executive caught our eye: "I've been around football for 40 years, and I've never met a guy [Angelichio] who is more obsessed with football." Breaking news: Guy who works in football ... likes football! This is earth-shattering stuff! Offensive Coordinator Brian Fleury, SEA After years working as the TEs coach for Kyle Shanahan in San Francisco, Fleury joins an NFC West division rival, inheriting the big shoes of Klint Kubiak. It does help that Fleury worked with Sam Darnold when he was a 49er in 2023, and this might be one of the most well-run organizations in football. Keep in mind, Seattle was incredibly healthy all year long with the third fewest “games lost” due to injury in the NFL. Offensive Coordinator Zac Robinson, TB After two years calling plays in Atlanta, Robinson linked up with division rival Tampa Bay, becoming Baker Mayfield’s fifth different offensive coordinator over the last five years. The Buccaneers suffered multiple injuries on offense last year, and Baker averaged the lowest yards per attempt (4.99) versus man coverage in the league. Nevertheless, in a weak NFC South division, the Buccaneers can still make noise with some of their young offensive playmakers. Offensive Coordinator Brian Daboll, TEN The Titans were straight diaper gravy on offense last year, ranking 30th in points per game and 31st in yards per game. Daboll’s success as a play-caller should make Cam Ward a great bet for a sophomore step forward. Over the last decade, QBs drafted in the top 10 averaged 2.6 more fantasy points per game in Year 2. Expect a higher pass rate and a chance for multiple pass-catchers to enter the fantasy conversation, something we could not say last year in Tennessee. Offensive Coordinator David Blough, WAS At just 30 years old, Blough is the second youngest OC in the NFL considering he was a backup QB in the league as recently as 2023! He steps into an incredible spot as Jayden Daniels’ play-caller after being the team's QB coach under Kliff Kingsbury. After Daniels and Terry McLaurin appeared in just three total games together in 2025, we can expect better luck in 2026. Washington quietly has been effective running the ball the last few years, so the key factors in the offense will be the emergence of another pass-catcher opposite Terry. Will that be free agent signee Chig Okonkwo or third-round rookie Antonio Williams?
